As a member of the royal family, Neferkare IV was known for his diplomatic efforts to strengthen ties with neighboring kingdoms. He also oversaw major architectural projects, including the construction of temples and palaces throughout Egypt.

Despite his significance in ancient Egyptian history, Neferkare IV's legacy is somewhat overshadowed by that of his predecessor and successor. Nevertheless, his contributions to Egyptian culture and politics are still studied and appreciated today.

A lasting testament to Neferkare IV's reign is the discovery of several well-preserved artifacts, including a golden funerary mask and a collection of ancient texts.

The impact of Neferkare IV's rule can be seen in the subsequent dynasties that followed him, which continued to build upon his achievements and expand Egypt's influence throughout the ancient world.
